prompts: Create {WS}/scene/index.html: a single-file 3D scene with three.js 0.170.0 loaded from https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js (an import map is fine), in low poly or voxel style, showing the classic view of Mount Fuji with the Chureito pagoda (red, five tiers) and cherry trees in bloom in the foreground, with an atmospheric sky (dusk or haze). All geometry must be procedural (no external models or textures). The camera must frame the composition on load; include a subtle animation. This is your ONLY request: there will be no second turn and no answers to questions. Deliver the complete, working final file. Work only inside {WS}.
answers:
[goal] Create `./scene/index.html`, a single-file three.js 0.170.0 scene of Mount Fuji with the Chureito pagoda and cherry trees at dusk.

[action] I wrote `scene/index.html`. It loads three.js through an import map from the jsDelivr URL you gave. All geometry is procedural, with no external models or textures.
- **Sky:** a dusk gradient shader with a low sun, glow and twinkling stars.
- **Fuji:** a faceted low-poly cone with a snow cap and an irregular snow line, set against a haze-colored fog.
- **Pagoda:** red, five tiers, with dark roofs, upturned eave tips, glowing windows and a gold finial, on the left foreground hill.
- **Cherry trees:** voxel blossom canopies, foreground trees framing the view and smaller ones on the slope below.
- **Valley and hills:** a lake, a town with lit windows, pines on the hillsides, and drifting clouds.
- **Camera:** it is fixed to frame the pagoda, Fuji and the valley on load. Its field of view widens on narrow windows.
- **Animation:** it has a slow camera drift, tree sway, falling petals, drifting clouds, flickering window light and twinkling stars.

[result] A syntax check passed. I extracted the module script and ran `node --check`, which printed `SYNTAX_OK`. I did not render the scene in a browser, so the framing and colors are untested. I also left a scratch file at `tmp/check.mjs`, which can be deleted.

[next] Open `scene/index.html` in a browser with internet access, because the three.js module loads from the CDN.
